Always: helm diff upgrade → review → helm upgrade --dry-run → helm upgrade --atomic --wait --timeout 10m. The atomic flag is your safety net — failed upgrade = automatic rollback.

🔧
Finding Stale Releases

helm list --all --all-namespaces shows everything including failed and pending. helm list --failed -A finds broken releases. Clean up with helm uninstall or fix with helm rollback.

Release Management Decision Flowchart
  Release broken? ──YES──▶ helm rollback <name> ──SUCCESS──▶ 🎉 Done!
       │                                 │
       NO                               FAILED
       │                                 │
       ▼                                 ▼
  Everything OK?              helm uninstall --keep-history
       │                      helm install <name> ./chart
       ▼
  🎉 Production healthy!

  🔑 GOLDEN RULE: Always test with --dry-run first.
     helm upgrade <name> ./chart --dry-run --debug

🔄 Common Release Management Workflows

Here are the patterns you'll use every day — and what the certification exam tests:

The Three Most Common Workflows
  WORKFLOW 1: Fresh Deploy                         WORKFLOW 2: Update in Place
  ──────────────────────                           ────────────────────────
  helm install anihpj ./chart \                    helm upgrade anihpj ./chart \
    -f values-prod.yaml \                            --set image.tag=v3.0 \
    -n production                                    --atomic --wait
    --create-namespace
    --atomic --wait                                WORKFLOW 3: CI/CD Idempotent
                                                   ────────────────────────
  RESULT: New release created                       helm upgrade --install anihpj \
  Status: deployed                                    ./chart -f values-prod.yaml \
                                                       -n production \
                                                       --atomic --wait --timeout 10m

                                                   RESULT: Installs OR upgrades
                                                   Perfect for CI/CD pipelines!
🚀
First Deploy

helm install <name> ./chart -f values.yaml -n <ns> --create-namespace --atomic --wait

🔄
Update Config

helm upgrade <name> ./chart -f new-values.yaml --atomic --wait

⏪
Emergency Rollback

helm rollback <name> <revision> --wait

🔧
Safe Preview

helm upgrade <name> ./chart --dry-run --debug
Always preview before applying!

📥installCreate a new release
🔄upgradeUpdate existing release
⏪rollbackGo to previous revision
🗑️uninstallRemove a release
📋listView all releases
🔍statusCurrent release state

5.10 Release History & Rollback Strategy

Release Revision Timeline
RELEASE: anihpj-prod (namespace: production)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
REV  STATUS       DEPLOYED    CHART    APP VER   DESCRIPTION
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1    SUPERSEDED   10:00 AM    0.1.0    v1.0.0    Initial install
2    SUPERSEDED   10:30 AM    0.1.1    v1.0.1    Bug fix
3    SUPERSEDED   11:00 AM    0.2.0    v2.0.0    Major upgrade
4    FAILED       11:15 AM    0.2.1    v2.0.1    BROKEN - rolled back
5    DEPLOYED     11:16 AM    0.2.0    v2.0.0    Rollback to rev 3 ← CURRENT

MAX HISTORY: 10 (default) — oldest revisions auto-deleted!
Set with: helm install --history-max 20

ROLLBACK COMMANDS:
helm rollback anihpj-prod 3 -n production     # Go to revision 3
helm rollback anihpj-prod 0 -n production     # Rollback to PREVIOUS
helm rollback anihpj-prod --wait -n production # Rollback + wait for ready

KEY INSIGHT: helm rollback CREATES a new revision (6) with
the config from revision 3. Revision 3 is not re-activated.

5.11 --reuse-values vs --reset-values - Critical Difference

❌ --reuse-values (DANGER)

Reuses ALL previously set values (including --set values from last install). Can cause unexpected config if you forget what was set before.

# First install:
helm install app ./chart --set image.tag=v1.0
# Later upgrade (INTENT: change replicas only):
helm upgrade app ./chart --reuse-values --set replicaCount=5
# RESULT: image.tag STILL v1.0 (reused!) + replicaCount=5
✅ --reset-values (SAFE)

Discards ALL previous --set values. Uses ONLY what is in the chart's values.yaml + new -f files + new --set values.

# First install:
helm install app ./chart --set image.tag=v1.0
# Later upgrade (INTENT: start fresh):
helm upgrade app ./chart --reset-values -f values-v2.yaml
# RESULT: ALL previous --set values discarded.
# Only values-v2.yaml + chart defaults used.
⚠️
Exam Gotcha: If the question says "upgrade the release but keep all previously configured values," use --reuse-values. If it says "start fresh with new values," use --reset-values. These flags are mutually exclusive — you can't use both.

5.12 Release Status Codes - What Each Means

StatusMeaningCan helm install?Recovery Action
deployedRelease is running normally❌ Name in useUse helm upgrade
failedInstall/upgrade failed❌ Name in usehelm rollback or helm uninstall
supersededOld revision replaced by newerN/A (historical)Rollback target
pending-installInstall in progress❌ LockedWait or delete pending secret
pending-upgradeUpgrade in progress❌ LockedWait or delete pending secret
pending-rollbackRollback in progress❌ LockedWait or delete pending secret
uninstalledRelease removed✅ Can re-installUse helm install (name is free)
unknownHelm can't determine stateCheck historyInvestigate release secrets
Q1
What command installs a chart and creates a new release named "anihpj-prod" in the "production" namespace?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

helm install anihpj-prod ./anihpj-chart -n production --create-namespace

Explanation

On the exam, namespace accuracy is critical. Wrong namespace = 0 points. Always read questions carefully for namespace requirements. Use -n <ns> explicitly. Verify with kubectl config view --minify.

Q2
What does --atomic do during install or upgrade?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

If the operation fails, Helm automatically rolls back to the previous successful state. All-or-nothing.

Explanation

On the exam, namespace accuracy is critical. Wrong namespace = 0 points. Always read questions carefully for namespace requirements. Use -n <ns> explicitly. Verify with kubectl config view --minify.

Q3
How do you upgrade a release and keep all previously set values?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

helm upgrade anihpj ./chart --reuse-values. This keeps all existing values and only applies new chart defaults for new fields.

Explanation

--atomic auto-rolls back on failure — your safety net. Combine with --wait --timeout. Without it, failed releases stay broken. Essential for production and exam deployments.

Q4
What is the three-way merge in Helm 3?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

Helm compares (1) old manifest, (2) new manifest, and (3) live state in K8s to determine what to change. Prevents overwriting changes made by other controllers.

Explanation

This concept is frequently tested on the Helm certification exam. The illustration below demonstrates the practical application with real commands and examples you can use directly in the exam terminal.

# Standard install command:
helm install RELEASE ./chart -n NAMESPACE --create-namespace

# Install with values file:
helm install RELEASE ./chart -f values.yaml -n NAMESPACE

# Install with --set overrides:
helm install RELEASE ./chart --set image.tag=v2.0 -n NAMESPACE

# Install with --atomic (auto-rollback on failure):
helm install RELEASE ./chart -n NAMESPACE --atomic --wait --timeout 5m
Q5
How do you rollback to revision 2 of a release?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

helm rollback anihpj 2. Use helm history anihpj first to see available revisions.

Explanation

This concept is frequently tested on the Helm certification exam. The illustration below demonstrates the practical application with real commands and examples you can use directly in the exam terminal.

# Rollback to previous revision:
helm rollback RELEASE -n NAMESPACE

# Rollback to specific revision:
helm rollback RELEASE 3 -n NAMESPACE

# View history first:
helm history RELEASE -n NAMESPACE
# 1  Tue Jan 15 10:00:00 2024  SUPERSEDED  anihpj-0.1.0  1.0.0  Install complete
# 2  Tue Jan 15 10:30:00 2024  SUPERSEDED  anihpj-0.1.1  1.0.1  Upgrade complete
# 3  Tue Jan 15 11:00:00 2024  FAILED      anihpj-0.2.0  2.0.0  Upgrade failed

# Rollback creates a NEW revision:
helm rollback RELEASE 2 -n NAMESPACE
# Creates revision 4 with config from revision 2
Q6
What is the default maximum number of stored revisions?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

10 revisions. Increase with --history-max flag. Beyond the limit, oldest revisions are deleted and cannot be rolled back to.

Explanation

This concept is frequently tested on the Helm certification exam. The illustration below demonstrates the practical application with real commands and examples you can use directly in the exam terminal.

# Release storage (per revision):
kubectl get secrets -l owner=helm -n NAMESPACE
# sh.helm.release.v1.anihpj.v1
# sh.helm.release.v1.anihpj.v2
# sh.helm.release.v1.anihpj.v3

# Each Secret contains:
# - Chart metadata (name, version)
# - Computed values (all overrides merged)
# - Rendered manifests (the actual YAML applied)
# - Release info (status, timestamps)

# Inspect a revision:
kubectl get secret sh.helm.release.v1.anihpj.v2 -n prod -o jsonpath='{.data.release}' | base64 -d | gzip -d | python -m json.tool
Q7
How do you uninstall a release but keep its history?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

helm uninstall anihpj --keep-history. The release status becomes "uninstalled" but history records remain.

Explanation

default is the #1 safety function: {{ .Values.x | default "safe" }}. Prevents nil pointer panics — the most common Helm error. Every nullable value reference needs this.

Q8
What command makes install/upgrade idempotent for CI/CD?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

helm upgrade --install anihpj ./chart. Installs if release doesn't exist, upgrades if it does — safe for repeated pipeline runs.

Explanation

This concept is frequently tested on the Helm certification exam. The illustration below demonstrates the practical application with real commands and examples you can use directly in the exam terminal.

# Standard upgrade:
helm upgrade RELEASE ./chart -n NAMESPACE

# Upgrade with new values:
helm upgrade RELEASE ./chart -f values-new.yaml -n NAMESPACE

# Upgrade-or-install (idempotent):
helm upgrade --install RELEASE ./chart -n NAMESPACE

# Upgrade with auto-rollback:
helm upgrade RELEASE ./chart -n NAMESPACE --atomic --cleanup-on-fail
Q9
What does helm get values show vs helm get values --all?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

helm get values = user-supplied values only. --all = user values + chart defaults merged. The difference helps debug configuration issues.

Explanation

helm get inspects deployed releases: values (user-supplied), values --all (merged), manifest (rendered YAML), hooks, notes. Essential for debugging configuration and drift.

Q10
A release is in "failed" state. How do you view what went wrong?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

helm status anihpj shows current state and error messages. helm history anihpj shows revision history. helm get all anihpj --revision <n> shows the failed revision's details.

Explanation

This concept is frequently tested on the Helm certification exam. The illustration below demonstrates the practical application with real commands and examples you can use directly in the exam terminal.

# Hook annotations on a Job resource:
metadata:
  annotations:
    "helm.sh/hook": pre-upgrade          # Hook type
    "helm.sh/hook-weight": "-5"          # Execution order
    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": hook-succeeded

# Available hook types:
# pre-install, post-install, pre-upgrade, post-upgrade,
# pre-delete, post-delete, pre-rollback, post-rollback, test

# Weights: Lower numbers execute FIRST
# Deletion policies: hook-succeeded, hook-failed, before-hook-creation

Chapter 6: Go Templating Fundamentals — The YAML Generation Engine

Templates are where Helm transforms from a simple package manager into a powerful code generator. Using Go's text/template library with Sprig's 70+ functions, you write templates that produce different Kubernetes YAML based on values, conditions, and loops. This chapter covers the foundational building blocks.

🟡 Intermediate ⏱️ ~2 hours 🔧 Core 🎯 25% Exam Weight

🎯 What You'll Learn

  • ✅ Master the {{ }} template syntax and delimiter rules
  • ✅ Understand all Built-in Objects: .Release, .Values, .Chart, .Files, .Capabilities
  • ✅ Access nested configuration through the .Values object
  • ✅ Use release metadata through the .Release object
  • ✅ Embed static files and detect K8s capabilities
🎓 Certification Domains
Templates 25% Built-in Objects FOUNDATION
Template Rendering Pipeline — How YAML is Generated
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  TEMPLATE RENDERING PIPELINE                                  │
  │                                                                │
  │  ┌──────────┐   ┌──────────┐   ┌──────────────┐             │
  │  │ values.  │   │ Template │   │ Rendered     │             │
  │  │ yaml     │──▶│ Engine   │──▶│ K8s YAML     │             │
  │  │ (config) │   │ (Go tmpl │   │ (final       │             │
  │  │          │   │  + Sprig)│   │  manifests)  │             │
  │  └──────────┘   └──────────┘   └──────┬───────┘             │
  │                                       │                      │
  │  ┌────────────────────────────────────▼───────────────────┐ │
  │  │  kubectl apply -f <rendered YAML>  (via K8s API)       │ │
  │  │  or helm install → renders + applies automatically     │ │
  │  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
  │                                                                │
  │  DEBUG: helm template ./chart --debug  → see rendered YAML   │
  │  DEBUG: helm install ./chart --dry-run → simulate install    │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

6.1 Template Syntax — {{ }} Delimiters

Helm templates use Go's text/template syntax. Everything between {{ and }} is evaluated as a template expression. Everything outside is literal text (YAML).

Template Syntax Basics
# This is a Helm template file (e.g., deployment.yaml)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-deployment    # ← Template expression
  labels:
    app: {{ .Chart.Name }}                # ← Chart name from Chart.yaml
spec:
  replicas: {{ .Values.replicaCount }}    # ← Value from values.yaml
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: {{ .Chart.Name }}
        image: "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}"
📖 Whitespace Control

Use {{- to trim leading whitespace and -}} to trim trailing whitespace. {{- .Values.name -}} removes spaces on both sides — crucial for clean YAML output.

6.2 Built-in Objects — The Template Context

Helm provides five built-in objects that give templates access to all configuration and metadata:

⚙️
.Values

All values from values.yaml, -f files, and --set flags. Your primary data source. Access nested keys with dot notation.

🚀
.Release

Information about the release: Name, Namespace, Revision, IsUpgrade, IsInstall, Service.

📦
.Chart

Metadata from Chart.yaml: Name, Version, AppVersion, Description, Type, ApiVersion.

📁
.Files

Access static files bundled in the chart (not in templates/). Useful for ConfigMaps with config files.

🔍
.Capabilities

Kubernetes cluster information: Version, API versions available. Use for version-conditional templates.

📋
.Template

Information about the current template: Name and BasePath of the file being rendered.

6.3 The .Values Object — Accessing Configuration

.Values is your primary interface to user-supplied configuration. It contains everything from values.yaml plus overrides.

Accessing .Values
# Given this values.yaml:
# replicaCount: 3
# image:
#   repository: anihpj/anihpj
#   tag: v2.1
# service:
#   port: 80

replicas: {{ .Values.replicaCount }}           # → 3
image: "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}"  # → anihpj/anihpj:v2.1
port: {{ .Values.service.port }}               # → 80

# Accessing a key that doesn't exist = RUNTIME ERROR
# Use default() for safety:
port: {{ .Values.service.port | default 8080 }}

6.4 The .Release Object — Name, Namespace, Revision

.Release Fields
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-anihpj       # Release name (e.g., anihpj-prod)
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}    # Target namespace
  annotations:
    revision: "{{ .Release.Revision }}"   # Current revision number
    isUpgrade: "{{ .Release.IsUpgrade }}" # true/false
    isInstall: "{{ .Release.IsInstall }}" # true/false
    service: {{ .Release.Service }}      # Always "Helm"

6.5 The .Chart Object — Metadata Access

Access Chart.yaml fields directly in templates. Useful for labels and annotations that should match chart metadata.

.Chart Usage
labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: {{ .Chart.Name }}
    app.kubernetes.io/version: {{ .Chart.AppVersion }}
    helm.sh/chart: {{ .Chart.Name }}-{{ .Chart.Version }}

6.6 The .Files Object — Embedding Static Files

Include files from your chart (config files, scripts, certificates) in ConfigMaps or Secrets.

.Files Examples
# Embed a file's content in a ConfigMap
data:
  nginx.conf: |
{{ .Files.Get "config/nginx.conf" | indent 4 }}

# Get file as base64 (for Secrets)
data:
  cert.pem: {{ .Files.Get "certs/cert.pem" | b64enc }}

# List all non-template files
{{ range $path, $_ := .Files.Glob "config/**" }}
  {{ $path }}: |
{{ $.Files.Get $path | indent 4 }}
{{ end }}

6.7 The .Capabilities Object — K8s Version & API Detection

Detect what your cluster supports at render time. Essential for backward-compatible charts.

.Capabilities Usage
# Check Kubernetes version
{{ if .Capabilities.KubeVersion.GitVersion }}
  # Running on Kubernetes {{ .Capabilities.KubeVersion.GitVersion }}
{{ end }}

# Check if an API version is available
{{ if .Capabilities.APIVersions.Has "networking.k8s.io/v1/Ingress" }}
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
{{ else }}
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1beta1
{{ end }}
kind: Ingress

🛡️ Go Template Gotchas & Best Practices

Common Template Pitfalls — And How to Avoid Them
  ❌ GOTCHA 1: Missing whitespace control
  ─────────────────────────────────────
  {{ .Values.name }}          → "  anihpj  " (extra whitespace!)
  {{- .Values.name -}}        → "anihpj"     (clean!)

  ❌ GOTCHA 2: Nil pointer when key doesn't exist
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  {{ .Values.missing }}       → CRASH: nil pointer evaluating...
  {{ .Values.missing | default "safe" }} → "safe"

  ❌ GOTCHA 3: Scope loss inside with/range
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  {{ with .Values.db }}
    name: {{ .host }}         ✅ . is now .Values.db
    release: {{ .Release.Name }} ❌ .Release not accessible!
    release: {{ $.Release.Name }} ✅ Use $ for root scope
  {{ end }}

  ❌ GOTCHA 4: Forgetting to quote strings with special chars
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  value: {{ .Values.special }}   → YAML parse error if ":" in value
  value: {{ .Values.special | quote }} → safe!
🛡️
Always use default()

Never assume a key exists. {{ .Values.x | default "fallback" }} prevents nil pointer panics. This is the #1 cause of template errors.

🛡️
Always quote dynamic strings

{{ .Values.name | quote }} wraps in double quotes. Prevents YAML parsing errors from special characters like colons, hashes, and brackets.

🛡️
Use $ for root scope

Inside with or range, $ always refers to the root context. {{ $.Release.Name }} works anywhere.

🛡️
Trim whitespace with {{- -}}

{{- eats leading whitespace, -}} eats trailing. Both: {{- .Values.x -}}. Critical for clean YAML.

🛡️
Use include, not template

include returns a string (pipeline-friendly). template writes inline (no pipelines). Always prefer include.

🛡️
nindent for block insertion

nindent N = newline + indent N spaces. Use when inserting YAML blocks: {{ include "labels" . | nindent 4 }}.

{{ }}DelimitersTemplate expression syntax
⚙️.ValuesUser configuration
🚀.ReleaseRelease metadata
📦.ChartChart metadata
📁.FilesStatic file access
🔍.CapabilitiesCluster API detection

6.8 Built-in Objects - Complete Reference

Every Helm template has access to these built-in objects. Understanding them is critical for the certification exam — you'll need to know exactly which object to use for common tasks.

ObjectKey PropertiesExample UsageWhen to Use
.Release.Name, .Namespace, .Revision, .IsUpgrade, .IsInstall, .Service{{ .Release.Name }}Release-specific metadata; labeling resources
.ValuesYour values.yaml structure{{ .Values.image.tag }}Accessing user configuration
.Chart.Name, .Version, .AppVersion, .Type, .ApiVersion{{ .Chart.Version }}Chart metadata in labels/annotations
.Files.Get(name), .GetBytes(name), .Glob(pattern), .AsConfig(), .AsSecrets(){{ .Files.Get "config.json" }}Embedding static files in ConfigMaps/Secrets
.Capabilities.KubeVersion, .APIVersions.Has(){{ .Capabilities.KubeVersion.GitVersion }}K8s version detection; API availability check
.Template.Name, .BasePath{{ .Template.Name }}Rarely used directly; template identification

6.9 Template Syntax - Beyond the Basics

Action Delimiters
  • {{ }} — Output something (renders to YAML)
  • {{- -}} — Trim whitespace (left/right/both)
  • {{/* */}} — Template comments (NOT in output)
  • {{ }} — Whitespace-sensitive
Whitespace Control

{{- .Values.name }} trims left whitespace. {{ .Values.name -}} trims right. {{- .Values.name -}} trims both. Always use - for clean YAML output!

Variable Assignment
  • {{ $var := "value" }} — Define variable
  • {{ $var = "new" }} — Reassign (no colon)
  • {{ range $i, $v := .List }} — Loop index+value
  • {{ with $val := .Nested }} — Scoped variable
# Common variable patterns:
{{ $fullName := include "anihpj.fullname" . }}
{{ $labels := include "anihpj.labels" . | nindent 4 }}

# In a range loop:
{{ range $env, $val := .Values.env }}
  - name: {{ $env }}
    value: {{ $val | quote }}
{{ end }}

6.10 The .Files Object - Embedding Static Content

The .Files object gives templates access to non-template files in the chart. This is essential for ConfigMaps containing configuration files, certificates, or scripts.

.Files Object Methods
CHART STRUCTURE
anihpj-chart/
  files/
    nginx.conf         .Files.Get "files/nginx.conf"
    app-config.json    .Files.Get "files/app-config.json"
    certs/
      tls.crt          .Files.Glob "certs/*"
      tls.key
  templates/
    configmap.yaml     Uses {{ .Files.Get }} to embed

.Files.Get "path"        Returns file content as string
.Files.GetBytes "path"   Returns file content as []byte
.Files.Glob "pattern"    Returns list of matching file paths
.Files.AsConfig "path"   Returns file(s) as ConfigMap-ready YAML
.Files.AsSecrets "path"  Returns file(s) as Secret-ready YAML
GOTCHA
Exam Gotcha: Files in .helmignore are NOT accessible via .Files. Also, .Files.Get throws an error if the file doesn't exist — use .Files.Glob to check existence first.

6.11 The .Capabilities Object - API Version Detection

One of the most powerful and exam-relevant built-in objects. .Capabilities lets templates detect the Kubernetes cluster version and available APIs at render time.

# Check Kubernetes version:
{{ if semverCompare ">=1.25-0" .Capabilities.KubeVersion.GitVersion }}
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1  # Use v1 Ingress (K8s 1.19+)
{{ else }}
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1beta1  # Legacy Ingress
{{ end }}

# Check if an API is available:
{{ if .Capabilities.APIVersions.Has "monitoring.coreos.com/v1" }}
# Deploy ServiceMonitor (Prometheus Operator is installed)
{{ end }}

# Check for specific resource:
{{ if .Capabilities.APIVersions.Has "autoscaling/v2/HorizontalPodAutoscaler" }}
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
{{ else }}
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2beta2
{{ end }}
EXAM
Exam Tip: Questions about API version compatibility are common. Always check the cluster's K8s version BEFORE deciding which API version to use. .Capabilities.KubeVersion.GitVersion returns something like v1.29.0 — use semverCompare for comparisons.

6.12 Understanding the Template Rendering Pipeline - Step by Step

When you run helm install, Helm doesn't just substitute values. It runs a full rendering pipeline that transforms templates + values into valid Kubernetes YAML. Understanding each step helps debug template issues.

1
Load Chart

Helm reads Chart.yaml, values.yaml, and ALL files in templates/ (recursively). Files matching .helmignore patterns are excluded. The chart is loaded into memory as a Go struct.

2
Build Values

Helm merges values in precedence order: chart's values.yaml → parent chart values → -f files (in order) → --set overrides. This produces a single merged .Values object.

3
Execute Templates

Each file in templates/ is processed by Go's text/template engine with the Sprig function library. The . (dot) is set to the root context containing .Values, .Release, .Chart, .Files, .Capabilities, and .Template.

4
Concatenate & Parse as YAML

All rendered template output is concatenated into one big YAML stream. Helm parses this stream to extract individual Kubernetes resource objects (separated by ---).

5
Sort & Apply

Resources are sorted by kind (Namespaces first, then Secrets, ConfigMaps, Services, Deployments, etc.). This ensures dependencies are created in the right order. Then kubectl apply is called for each resource.

6
Store Release

The rendered manifest, computed values, and chart metadata are compressed, base64-encoded, and stored as a Kubernetes Secret named sh.helm.release.v1.<name>.v<rev>.

6.13 The Dot (.) - Helm's Most Important Concept

In Go templates, . (dot) is the current context. It changes meaning depending on where you are in the template. Mastering the dot is essential for writing correct templates.

How the Dot Changes Context
DOT CONTEXT VISUALIZATION
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

TOP LEVEL:
{{ .Values.image.tag }}    . = {Values: {...}, Release: {...}, Chart: {...}}
                              ↑
                          The ENTIRE root object

INSIDE with:
{{ with .Values.image }}     . = .Values.image = {repository: "anihpj", tag: "v2.0"}
  {{ .repository }}          .repository = "anihpj" ✓ (dot is now image object)
  {{ .tag }}                 .tag = "v2.0" ✓
{{ end }}

INSIDE range:
{{ range .Values.env }}      . = each element of the env list
  {{ .name }}                .name = "DEBUG" (dot is the current env item)
  {{ .value }}               .value = "true"
{{ end }}

DOT IS REBOUND INSIDE: with, range, define blocks
DOT IS PRESERVED BY: if/else blocks

CRITICAL: Inside {{ range }}, you CANNOT access .Values anymore!
Because . now points to the loop variable, not the root.
FIX: Save the root: {{ $root := . }} before range, then use {{ $root.Values.xxx }}
⚠️
The #1 Template Error: Accessing .Values.something inside a range or with block without saving the root context first. Always do {{- $ := . -}} at the top of templates that use range/with to preserve access to the root.
Q1
What delimiters does Helm use for template expressions?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

{{ and }}. Everything between them is evaluated as a Go template expression. {{- trims leading whitespace, -}} trims trailing.

Explanation
  {{ .Values.name }}       ← Evaluates to the value of .Values.name
  {{ .Values.name | quote }} ← Piped through the quote function
  {{- .Values.name -}}     ← Trims whitespace on both sides

Whitespace control is critical for clean YAML output. Without {{- and -}}, template expressions leave blank lines that can break YAML parsing.

Explanation

This concept is frequently tested on the Helm certification exam. The illustration below demonstrates the practical application with real commands and examples you can use directly in the exam terminal.

# template vs include - Key Difference:

# template: writes directly to output (NO piping)
{{ template "mylib.labels" . }}

# include: returns a string (CAN pipe through functions)
{{ include "mylib.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
{{ include "mylib.labels" . | quote }}

# Named template definition:
{{- define "anihpj.labels" -}}
app.kubernetes.io/name: {{ .Chart.Name }}
app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
{{- end }}

# Usage:
metadata:
  labels:
    {{- include "anihpj.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
Q11
What does {{- (dash) do in a template?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

The dash - trims whitespace. {{- trims LEFT whitespace. -}} trims RIGHT. {{- ... -}} trims BOTH. Without the dash, extra newlines appear in rendered YAML.

Explanation

Whitespace control is critical for clean YAML output. Always use {{- and -}} at template boundaries. The dash chomps the adjacent whitespace including newlines.

Q12
How do you access a file's content inside a template?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

Use {{ .Files.Get "config.json" }}. Returns file content as string. .Files.GetBytes returns bytes. .Files.Glob "*.json" matches patterns. Files must be in the chart directory and NOT excluded by .helmignore.

Explanation

.Files.Get throws an error if the file doesn't exist — check with .Files.Glob first. .Files.AsConfig and .Files.AsSecrets produce ConfigMap/Secret-ready YAML automatically.

Q13
What is the difference between .Chart.Version and .Chart.AppVersion?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

.Chart.Version = chart's SemVer version (required). .Chart.AppVersion = application version (optional, informational). Change chart version on every chart change; appVersion when the application inside changes.

Explanation

Chart version drives Helm upgrades. AppVersion is just metadata — useful for labeling: app.kubernetes.io/version: {{ .Chart.AppVersion }}. Both come from Chart.yaml.

Q14
How do you conditionally include a resource using if?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

Wrap the entire resource in {{ if .Values.ingress.enabled }}...{{ end }}. When the condition is false, the resource is completely omitted from rendered output. Use this for optional resources like Ingress, HPA, and PVC.

Explanation

This is the standard pattern for optional resources. The condition checks a boolean from values.yaml. Combine with else for alternative resources: {{ if .Values.tls }}...secure config...{{ else }}...basic config...{{ end }}.

Q15
What are .Release.IsInstall and .Release.IsUpgrade?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

Booleans indicating the current operation type. .Release.IsInstall is true during helm install. .Release.IsUpgrade is true during helm upgrade. Both are false during helm template (no cluster interaction).

Explanation

Use these to differentiate install vs upgrade behavior: run migrations only on fresh installs, skip certain resources on upgrades, show different NOTES.txt messages. .Release.Revision also increments on each install/upgrade/rollback.

Q2
Name three Built-in Objects available in Helm templates.
Answer & Explanation
Answer

.Values, .Release, .Chart, .Files, .Capabilities. Each provides different contextual data to templates.

Explanation

These five objects plus .Template form the complete template context. Every Go template function (if, range, with) operates within this context. The dot (.) represents the current scope — initially the root context containing all built-in objects. Inside with or range blocks, . changes, but $ always refers to the root.

Explanation

helm template renders YAML locally without a cluster. Unlike --dry-run, it skips API validation. Use --debug for detailed output. Ideal for CI/CD and offline development.

Q3
How do you access a nested value like image.tag from values.yaml?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

{{ .Values.image.tag }}. Use dot notation to traverse nested keys. For safety: {{ .Values.image.tag | default "latest" }}.

Explanation

Given image: { repository: anihpj, tag: v2.1 } in values.yaml, .Values.image returns the entire map, and .Values.image.tag drills down to "v2.1". Dot notation chains through nested YAML structures. The default function prevents nil pointer panics when a key doesn't exist — a must-use safety pattern.

Explanation

values.yaml provides defaults accessed via .Values. Best practices: comment keys, flat nesting, sensible defaults, never store secrets. Override with --set (highest) or -f files.

Q4
How do you embed a file from the chart into a ConfigMap?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

{{ .Files.Get "path/to/file" | indent 4 }}. Place the file in your chart (not in templates/) and reference it with .Files.Get.

Explanation

This concept is frequently tested on the Helm certification exam. The illustration below demonstrates the practical application with real commands and examples you can use directly in the exam terminal.

# values.yaml with documented defaults:
replicaCount: 3
image:
  repository: anihpj        # Docker image repository
  tag: v2.0.0                # Image tag (pin in production!)
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent   # Image pull policy

service:
  type: ClusterIP            # ClusterIP | NodePort | LoadBalancer
  port: 80                   # Service port

ingress:
  enabled: true              # Enable/disable Ingress resource
  className: nginx           # Ingress class name
  host: anihpj.example.com   # Ingress hostname
  tls: true                  # Enable TLS

# Access in templates: {{ .Values.replicaCount }}
# Override: --set replicaCount=5
Q5
How do you check if the cluster supports a specific Kubernetes API version?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

{{ if .Capabilities.APIVersions.Has "networking.k8s.io/v1/Ingress" }}...{{ end }}. Use this for version-conditional templates.

Explanation

This concept is frequently tested on the Helm certification exam. The illustration below demonstrates the practical application with real commands and examples you can use directly in the exam terminal.

# template vs include - Key Difference:

# template: writes directly to output (NO piping)
{{ template "mylib.labels" . }}

# include: returns a string (CAN pipe through functions)
{{ include "mylib.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
{{ include "mylib.labels" . | quote }}

# Named template definition:
{{- define "anihpj.labels" -}}
app.kubernetes.io/name: {{ .Chart.Name }}
app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
{{- end }}

# Usage:
metadata:
  labels:
    {{- include "anihpj.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
Q6
What does .Release.IsUpgrade return?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

true if the current operation is an upgrade, false if it's a fresh install. Used to conditionally run upgrade-only logic.

Explanation

This concept is frequently tested on the Helm certification exam. The illustration below demonstrates the practical application with real commands and examples you can use directly in the exam terminal.

# Key exam commands to remember:
helm lint ./chart --strict
helm template test ./chart --debug
helm install test ./chart --dry-run --debug
helm install prod ./chart -f values.yaml -n NAMESPACE --atomic --wait
helm list -A
helm history RELEASE -n NAMESPACE
helm get manifest RELEASE -n NAMESPACE
helm rollback RELEASE -n NAMESPACE
helm test RELEASE -n NAMESPACE --logs
Q7
How do you reference the chart name from Chart.yaml in a template?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

{{ .Chart.Name }}. Also available: .Chart.Version, .Chart.AppVersion, .Chart.ApiVersion.

Explanation

Chart.yaml requires: apiVersion: v2, name, version. Critical: version (chart) and appVersion (app) are INDEPENDENT. type: application (deployable) or library (template-only).

Q8
What happens if you reference .Values.missingKey when the key doesn't exist?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

Runtime error: template rendering fails with "nil pointer evaluating interface." Always use default: {{ .Values.missingKey | default "fallback" }}.

Explanation

This concept is frequently tested on the Helm certification exam. The illustration below demonstrates the practical application with real commands and examples you can use directly in the exam terminal.

# Minimal valid Chart.yaml:
apiVersion: v2
name: mychart
version: 0.1.0
type: application

# Full Chart.yaml reference:
apiVersion: v2
name: anihpj
version: 0.2.0
appVersion: "2.1.0"
description: A Helm chart for the anihpj job board application
type: application
kubeVersion: ">=1.25.0-0"
maintainers:
  - name: DevOps Team
    email: devops@example.com
icon: https://example.com/anihpj-icon.svg
keywords:
  - django
  - job-board
  - python
Q9
How do you base64-encode a file's content for a Secret?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

{{ .Files.Get "certs/cert.pem" | b64enc }}. b64enc is a Sprig function that encodes strings to base64.

Explanation

Never store plaintext secrets in values.yaml. Use placeholders, inject at deploy time (--set or CI/CD), encode with b64enc in templates. Production: Sealed Secrets, External Secrets Operator, or Vault.

Q10
What objects would you use to generate Kubernetes-standard labels?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

Use .Chart.Name, .Chart.Version, and .Release.Name for standard K8s labels: app.kubernetes.io/name, helm.sh/chart, app.kubernetes.io/instance.

Explanation

Never store plaintext secrets in values.yaml. Use placeholders, inject at deploy time (--set or CI/CD), encode with b64enc in templates. Production: Sealed Secrets, External Secrets Operator, or Vault.

Chapter 7: Template Functions & Pipelines — The Power Tools

Go templates alone are limited. Helm supercharges them with 70+ Sprig functions plus custom Helm functions. This chapter covers string manipulation, type conversion, control structures (if/range/with), named templates, pipelines, and the tpl function — everything you need to write sophisticated, reusable templates.

🟡 Intermediate ⏱️ ~3 hours 🔧 Functions 🎯 25% Exam Weight

🎯 What You'll Learn

  • ✅ Master string, type, math, and date transformation functions
  • ✅ Use default, required, and empty for safe value handling
  • ✅ Control template flow with if/else, with, and range
  • ✅ Create reusable templates with define, template, and include
  • ✅ Chain functions with pipelines |
  • ✅ Evaluate templates dynamically with tpl
  • ✅ Debug templates effectively
🎓 Certification Domains
Templates 25% Functions & Pipelines HEAVILY TESTED

7.1 String Functions

String Functions
# quote: Wrap in double quotes (safe for YAML strings with special chars)
name: {{ .Values.appName | quote }}               # → "anihpj"

# upper / lower: Case conversion
{{ "anihpj" | upper }}                            # → ANIHPJ
{{ "ANIHpj" | lower }}                            # → anihpj

# trim: Remove whitespace from both ends
{{ "  hello  " | trim }}                          # → "hello"

# replace: Replace substring (old new string)
{{ "anihpj-v1" | replace "-" "_" }}               # → "anihpj_v1"

# nospace: Remove all whitespace
{{ "a n i h p j" | nospace }}                     # → "anihpj"

# trunc: Truncate to N characters
{{ "anihpj-production-deployment" | trunc 10 }}   # → "anihpj-pro"

# indent: Indent every line by N spaces
data:
  config.yaml: |
{{ .Files.Get "config.yaml" | indent 4 }}

7.2 Type Conversion

Type Conversion Functions
# toYaml: Convert object to YAML string
{{ .Values.resources | toYaml | indent 10 }}
# Output:
#           limits:
#             cpu: 500m
#             memory: 256Mi

# fromYaml: Parse YAML string to object
{{ $config := .Files.Get "config.yaml" | fromYaml }}
port: {{ $config.server.port }}

# toJson / fromJson: Same but for JSON
{{ .Values.annotations | toJson }}
{{ $data := .Files.Get "data.json" | fromJson }}

# toString: Force-convert to string
{{ 42 | toString }}                              # → "42"

7.3 Default Values — Safety Nets

Default Value Functions
# default: Use fallback if value is empty/nil
replicas: {{ .Values.replicaCount | default 2 }}
image: {{ .Values.image.repository | default "nginx" }}

# required: FAIL if value is empty (for mandatory values)
{{ required "image.repository is required!" .Values.image.repository }}

# empty: Returns true if value is "empty" (0, "", nil, false, empty list/map)
{{ if empty .Values.tolerations }}
  # No tolerations configured
{{ end }}

# coalesce: Return first non-empty value from a list
{{ coalesce .Values.customName .Chart.Name "default-name" }}

7.4 Math Functions

Math Functions
# Basic arithmetic
{{ add 2 3 }}         # → 5
{{ sub 10 3 }}        # → 7
{{ mul 3 4 }}         # → 12
{{ div 10 2 }}        # → 5
{{ mod 10 3 }}        # → 1

# min / max: Find min or max of values
{{ min 1 5 3 9 }}     # → 1
{{ max 1 5 3 9 }}     # → 9

# Example: Calculate percentage
cpuPercent: {{ div .Values.usedCPU .Values.totalCPU | mul 100 }}

7.5 Date Functions

Date Functions
# now: Current date/time (in template rendering time)
deployedAt: {{ now | quote }}

# date: Format a date (layout reference: Mon Jan 2 15:04:05 MST 2006)
{{ date "2006-01-02" now }}

# dateModify: Add/subtract time
{{ now | dateModify "-24h" | date "2006-01-02" }}

# htmlDate: ISO 8601 format
{{ now | htmlDate }}

7.6 Control Structures — if/else, with, range

Control structures let your templates make decisions, iterate over data, and scope values.

7.6a if/else — Conditional Resource Inclusion

if/else Examples
{{ if .Values.ingress.enabled }}
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
# ... ingress spec ...
{{ else }}
# Ingress disabled — no ingress resource created
{{ end }}

{{ if eq .Values.environment "production" }}
  replicas: 5
{{ else if eq .Values.environment "staging" }}
  replicas: 2
{{ else }}
  replicas: 1
{{ end }}

7.6b with — Scoping Values

with Examples
# with changes the scope (.) to the specified value
{{ with .Values.postgresql }}
  - name: POSTGRES_HOST
    value: {{ .host }}        # . now refers to .Values.postgresql
  - name: POSTGRES_PORT
    value: {{ .port | default 5432 | quote }}
{{ end }}

# If the value is empty/nil, the block is silently skipped
{{ with .Values.optionalConfig }}
  # This block only renders if optionalConfig is non-empty
{{ end }}

7.6c range — Iterating Over Lists & Maps

range Examples
# Iterate over a list
{{ range .Values.ingress.hosts }}
  - host: {{ .host | quote }}
    http:
      paths:
      {{ range .paths }}
        - path: {{ .path }}
          pathType: {{ .pathType }}
      {{ end }}
{{ end }}

# Iterate over a map (key, value)
{{ range $key, $value := .Values.env }}
  - name: {{ $key }}
    value: {{ $value | quote }}
{{ end }}

7.6d Variable Assignment — $var := value

Variable Assignment
# Assign a variable with :=
{{ $appName := .Chart.Name }}
{{ $releaseName := .Release.Name }}

# Use the variable
name: {{ $appName }}-{{ $releaseName }}

# Variables are scoped — use $ to access outer scope inside range
{{ $globalName := .Release.Name }}
{{ range .Values.services }}
  name: {{ $globalName }}-{{ .name }}
{{ end }}

⚖️ Comparison & Logical Operators Reference

OperatorMeaningExample
eqEqual{{ if eq .Values.env "production" }}
neNot equal{{ if ne .Values.env "dev" }}
ltLess than{{ if lt .Values.replicas 3 }}
gtGreater than{{ if gt .Values.replicas 1 }}
leLess than or equal{{ if le .Values.replicas 5 }}
geGreater than or equal{{ if ge .Values.memory 256 }}
andLogical AND{{ if and .Values.enabled .Values.ready }}
orLogical OR{{ if or .Values.debug .Values.verbose }}
notLogical NOT{{ if not .Values.disabled }}

7.7 Named Templates — define, template, include

7.7a define vs template vs include — Key Differences

DirectivePurposePipeline SupportUse Case
defineDeclare a named template blockN/ACreating reusable snippets
templateExecute a named template inline❌ No pipelineSimple inclusion
includeExecute + return as string✅ Yes, pipe to indent, quote, etc.Always use include!
Named Template Example (_helpers.tpl)
{{/* _helpers.tpl */}}
{{- define "anihpj.fullname" -}}
{{- .Release.Name }}-{{ .Chart.Name }}
{{- end -}}

{{/* Usage in deployment.yaml */}}
name: {{ include "anihpj.fullname" . }}
# include returns a string — you can pipe it:
name: {{ include "anihpj.fullname" . | trunc 63 | quote }}

7.8 Pipelines — Chaining Functions with |

Pipeline Examples
# Chain multiple functions with |
{{ .Values.appName | upper | quote }}
# → "ANIHPJ"

# Common pipeline: get → indent
data:
  config.yaml: |
{{ .Files.Get "config.yaml" | indent 4 }}

# Complex pipeline: get → fromYaml → toYaml → indent
{{ .Files.Get "config.yaml" | fromYaml | toYaml | indent 4 }}

# Default + quote pipeline
{{ .Values.image.tag | default "latest" | quote }}

7.9 The tpl Function — Template Inside Template

tpl evaluates a string as a template. This lets users provide template expressions in values.yaml that are rendered at deploy time. Powerful but use sparingly.

tpl Examples
# values.yaml:
# greeting: "Hello, {{ .Values.name }}!"
# name: "World"

# template:
{{ tpl .Values.greeting . }}
# → "Hello, World!"

7.10 Template Debugging

Debug Commands

# Lint for syntax errors

# Simulate install/upgrade

helm upgrade test ./chart --dry-run --debug

7.11 Lookup Function — Querying K8s API at Render Time

The lookup function queries the Kubernetes API during template rendering. Use it to read existing resources. Warning: This breaks Helm's declarative model — use sparingly.

lookup Examples
# Check if a Secret exists
{{ $secret := lookup "v1" "Secret" .Release.Namespace "anihpj-credentials" }}
{{ if $secret }}
  # Secret exists, use existing value
{{ else }}
  # Secret doesn't exist yet
{{ end }}

7.14 Pipeline Patterns - Chaining for Clean Templates

Common Pipeline Chains
VALUE EXTRACTION + FORMATTING PATTERNS:
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

{{ .Values.image.tag | default "latest" | quote }}
    │                    │                   │
    └─ get value         └─ fallback         └─ wrap in quotes
    Result: "v2.0" or "latest"

{{ include "anihpj.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    │                            │
    └─ render named template     └─ indent 4 + newline
    Result: (indented label block)

{{ .Values.config | toYaml | indent 8 }}
    │                   │           │
    └─ get object       └─ to YAML  └─ indent 8 spaces
    Result: (indented YAML for ConfigMap data)

{{ range .Values.env }}
  - name: {{ .name | upper | quote }}
    value: {{ .value | quote }}
{{ end }}
    │            │        │
    └─ iterate   └─ upper └─ quote
    Result: (list of uppercased, quoted env vars)

7.16 Chart Development Tips & Tricks (from Official Docs)

These are battle-tested techniques from Helm chart maintainers, compiled from the official Chart Development Tips and Tricks guide.

Using the tpl Function — Template Inside a Template

The tpl function evaluates a string AS a template. This is powerful for injecting template strings via values or external files.

How tpl Works
# values.yaml
templateString: "{{ .Values.name }}"
name: "Tom"

# Template:
evaluated: {{ tpl .Values.templateString . }}
# Output: evaluated: Tom

# ADVANCED: Rendering external config files
# values.yaml:
firstName: Peter
lastName: Parker

# files/conf/app.conf:
firstName={{ .Values.firstName }}
lastName={{ .Values.lastName }}

# Template:
{{ tpl (.Files.Get "conf/app.conf") . }}
# Output:
firstName=Peter
lastName=Parker
Creating Image Pull Secrets Automatically
# values.yaml
imageCredentials:
  registry: quay.io
  username: someone
  password: sillyness
  email: someone@host.com

# _helpers.tpl
{{- define "imagePullSecret" }}
{{- with .Values.imageCredentials }}
{{- printf "{\"auths\":{\"%s\":{\"username\":\"%s\",\"password\":\"%s\",\"email\":\"%s\",\"auth\":\"%s\"}}}" .registry .username .password .email (printf "%s:%s" .username .password | b64enc) | b64enc }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}

# templates/secret.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
type: kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson
data:
  .dockerconfigjson: {{ template "imagePullSecret" . }}
Automatically Rolling Deployments on Config Change

Use sha256sum in a Deployment annotation to trigger automatic pod restarts when ConfigMaps or Secrets change:

kind: Deployment
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        checksum/config: {{ include (print $.Template.BasePath "/configmap.yaml") . | sha256sum }}
        checksum/secret: {{ include (print $.Template.BasePath "/secret.yaml") . | sha256sum }}
# Each time the ConfigMap or Secret changes, the Deployment's pod template
# annotation changes → triggers a rolling update automatically!
⚠️
Gotcha: In library charts, you cannot use $.Template.BasePath. Instead, use {{ include "mylibchart.configmap" . | sha256sum }} referencing the named template directly.
Preventing Helm from Uninstalling a Resource

The annotation helm.sh/resource-policy: keep tells Helm to NEVER delete this resource — even during helm uninstall. The resource becomes orphaned (no longer managed by Helm).

kind: Secret
metadata:
  annotations:
    "helm.sh/resource-policy": keep
  name: critical-data
# This Secret survives helm uninstall!
# WARNING: helm install --replace will conflict with orphaned resources
Q1
How do you provide a default value if .Values.replicas is not set?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

{{ .Values.replicas | default 3 }}. The default function returns the fallback if the value is nil, empty, or zero.

Explanation

default is the #1 safety function: {{ .Values.x | default "safe" }}. Prevents nil pointer panics — the most common Helm error. Every nullable value reference needs this.

Q2
What's the difference between template and include?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

template executes and writes inline (no pipeline support). include returns a string (supports pipelines like | indent, | quote). Always prefer include.

Explanation

include returns a string (pipeline-friendly: | indent). template writes inline (no pipelines). Always use include. This is a frequently tested exam concept.

Q3
How do you conditionally include a resource only in production?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

{{ if eq .Values.environment "production" }}...resource spec...{{ end }}. Use eq, ne, and, or, not for comparisons.

Explanation

Helm uses if for conditionals: {{ if .Values.ingress.enabled }}...{{ end }}. Wrap entire resources. Use eq, ne, lt, gt, and, or, not for comparisons. Resource-level conditionals are standard practice.

Q4
How do you iterate over a list of values in a template?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

{{ range .Values.ingress.hosts }}...{{ .host }}...{{ end }}. Inside range, . refers to the current item. For maps: {{ range $k, $v := .Values.env }}.

Explanation

This concept is frequently tested on the Helm certification exam. The illustration below demonstrates the practical application with real commands and examples you can use directly in the exam terminal.

# Standard install command:
helm install RELEASE ./chart -n NAMESPACE --create-namespace

# Install with values file:
helm install RELEASE ./chart -f values.yaml -n NAMESPACE

# Install with --set overrides:
helm install RELEASE ./chart --set image.tag=v2.0 -n NAMESPACE

# Install with --atomic (auto-rollback on failure):
helm install RELEASE ./chart -n NAMESPACE --atomic --wait --timeout 5m
Q5
How do you convert a values object to YAML inside a ConfigMap?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

{{ .Values.appConfig | toYaml | indent 4 }}. toYaml serializes the object, indent 4 adds proper indentation for ConfigMap data.

Explanation

This concept is frequently tested on the Helm certification exam. The illustration below demonstrates the practical application with real commands and examples you can use directly in the exam terminal.

# Key exam commands to remember:
helm lint ./chart --strict
helm template test ./chart --debug
helm install test ./chart --dry-run --debug
helm install prod ./chart -f values.yaml -n NAMESPACE --atomic --wait
helm list -A
helm history RELEASE -n NAMESPACE
helm get manifest RELEASE -n NAMESPACE
helm rollback RELEASE -n NAMESPACE
helm test RELEASE -n NAMESPACE --logs
Q6
What does tpl do?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

tpl evaluates a string as a template. {{ tpl .Values.dynamicGreeting . }} renders template expressions inside values at deploy time.

Explanation

This concept is frequently tested on the Helm certification exam. The illustration below demonstrates the practical application with real commands and examples you can use directly in the exam terminal.

# template vs include - Key Difference:

# template: writes directly to output (NO piping)
{{ template "mylib.labels" . }}

# include: returns a string (CAN pipe through functions)
{{ include "mylib.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
{{ include "mylib.labels" . | quote }}

# Named template definition:
{{- define "anihpj.labels" -}}
app.kubernetes.io/name: {{ .Chart.Name }}
app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
{{- end }}

# Usage:
metadata:
  labels:
    {{- include "anihpj.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
Q7
What function forces a value to be required (fail if missing)?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

{{ required "Error message" .Values.mandatoryKey }}. If mandatoryKey is empty/nil, Helm fails with the error message.

Explanation

required FAILS if the value is empty. Use for mandatory config: {{ required "msg" .Values.key }}. Opposite of default. Catches missing config before deployment.

Q8
How do you chain multiple functions together?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

Use the pipe | operator: {{ .Values.name | upper | quote }}. Each function's output becomes the next function's input.

Explanation

required FAILS if the value is empty. Use for mandatory config: {{ required "msg" .Values.key }}. Opposite of default. Catches missing config before deployment.

Q9
What does the lookup function do and when should you avoid it?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

lookup queries the K8s API at render time. Avoid it in most cases — it breaks Helm's declarative model and makes helm template fail (no API server available). Use values/config instead.

Explanation

This concept is frequently tested on the Helm certification exam. The illustration below demonstrates the practical application with real commands and examples you can use directly in the exam terminal.

# template vs include - Key Difference:

# template: writes directly to output (NO piping)
{{ template "mylib.labels" . }}

# include: returns a string (CAN pipe through functions)
{{ include "mylib.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
{{ include "mylib.labels" . | quote }}

# Named template definition:
{{- define "anihpj.labels" -}}
app.kubernetes.io/name: {{ .Chart.Name }}
app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
{{- end }}

# Usage:
metadata:
  labels:
    {{- include "anihpj.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
Q10
Where do you define named templates and what file extension do they use?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

In files starting with _ (like _helpers.tpl). Files starting with underscore are NOT deployed as K8s resources — they only contain reusable named templates.

Explanation

This concept is frequently tested on the Helm certification exam. The illustration below demonstrates the practical application with real commands and examples you can use directly in the exam terminal.

# template vs include - Key Difference:

# template: writes directly to output (NO piping)
{{ template "mylib.labels" . }}

# include: returns a string (CAN pipe through functions)
{{ include "mylib.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
{{ include "mylib.labels" . | quote }}

# Named template definition:
{{- define "anihpj.labels" -}}
app.kubernetes.io/name: {{ .Chart.Name }}
app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
{{- end }}

# Usage:

  labels:
    {{- include "anihpj.labels" . | nindent 4 }}

Chapter 8: Building the anihpj Chart Templates — Real-World Practice

Now we apply everything from Chapters 6 and 7 to build the complete anihpj chart. Each template below is a real, working example you can adapt for your own Django applications.

🟡 Intermediate ⏱️ ~2 hours 🛠️ Hands-On 🎯 25% Exam Weight

🎯 What You'll Learn

  • ✅ Build a parameterized Deployment template for Django
  • ✅ Create Service, ConfigMap, Secret, Ingress, and HPA templates
  • ✅ Write helpful NOTES.txt for post-install guidance
  • ✅ Create reusable helper functions in _helpers.tpl

8.1 Deployment Template — Parameterized for Flexibility

templates/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ include "anihpj.fullname" . }}
  labels: {{ include "anihpj.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
spec:
  replicas: {{ .Values.replicaCount }}
  selector:
    matchLabels: {{ include "anihpj.selectorLabels" . | nindent 6 }}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {{ include "anihpj.selectorLabels" . | nindent 8 }}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: {{ .Chart.Name }}
        image: "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}"
        imagePullPolicy: {{ .Values.image.pullPolicy }}
        ports:
        - containerPort: {{ .Values.service.port }}
        envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: {{ include "anihpj.fullname" . }}-config
        - secretRef:
            name: {{ include "anihpj.fullname" . }}-secret
        resources: {{ toYaml .Values.resources | nindent 10 }}

8.2 Service Template — Ports, Type, Selectors

templates/service.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: {{ include "anihpj.fullname" . }}
  labels: {{ include "anihpj.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
spec:
  type: {{ .Values.service.type }}
  ports:
  - port: {{ .Values.service.port }}
    targetPort: http
    protocol: TCP
  selector: {{ include "anihpj.selectorLabels" . | nindent 4 }}

8.3 ConfigMap Template — appSettings from values.yaml

templates/configmap.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: {{ include "anihpj.fullname" . }}-config
data:
  DEBUG: {{ .Values.config.debug | quote }}
  ALLOWED_HOSTS: {{ .Values.config.allowedHosts | quote }}
  DB_HOST: {{ .Release.Name }}-postgresql
  REDIS_HOST: {{ .Release.Name }}-redis-master

8.4 Secret Template — Database Credentials

templates/secret.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: {{ include "anihpj.fullname" . }}-secret
type: Opaque
data:
  SECRET_KEY: {{ .Values.config.secretKey | b64enc | quote }}
  DB_PASSWORD: {{ .Values.postgresql.auth.password | b64enc | quote }}

8.5 Ingress Template — Optional with Conditional

templates/ingress.yaml
{{ if .Values.ingress.enabled }}
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: {{ include "anihpj.fullname" . }}
spec:
  rules:
  {{ range .Values.ingress.hosts }}
  - host: {{ .host | quote }}
    http:
      paths:
      {{ range .paths }}
      - path: {{ .path }}
        pathType: {{ .pathType }}
        backend:
          service:
            name: {{ include "anihpj.fullname" $ }}
            port:
              number: {{ $.Values.service.port }}
      {{ end }}
  {{ end }}
{{ end }}

🐳 anihpj Dockerfile — The Container Behind the Chart

Helm deploys Kubernetes resources, but the actual application runs inside a container. Here's the Dockerfile that builds the anihpj (Django + jobpost) image referenced in our chart's values.yaml:

Dockerfile
# ─── anihpj Dockerfile ───
# Django Job Board Application with jobpost module
# Models: Skills, User, Author, Location, JobPost

FROM python:3.11-slim

# Set environment variables
ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    APP_HOME=/app

WORKDIR $APP_HOME

# Install system dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    gcc libpq-dev && \
    apt-get clean && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install Python dependencies
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Copy application code
COPY . .

# Collect static files
RUN python manage.py collectstatic --noinput

# Expose Django port
EXPOSE 8000

# Run with Gunicorn (production WSGI server)
CMD ["gunicorn", "anihpj.wsgi:application", "--bind", "0.0.0.0:8000", "--workers", "3"]
Build → Push → Deploy Pipeline
  ┌──────────┐     ┌──────────────┐     ┌──────────────────┐
  │ Docker   │     │ Container    │     │ Helm deploys     │
  │ Build    │────▶│ Registry     │────▶│ to Kubernetes    │
  │          │     │ (Docker Hub, │     │                  │
  │ docker   │     │  ACR, ECR,   │     │ helm install     │
  │ build -t │     │  GCR, etc.)  │     │ anihpj ./chart   │
  │ anihpj   │     │              │     │ --set image.tag  │
  │          │     │ docker push  │     │ =v2.1            │
  └──────────┘     └──────────────┘     └──────────────────┘

  🔑 The Docker image tag in values.yaml must match the tag you pushed!
     values.yaml: image.tag: "v2.1"  ← must match docker push tag

🧪 Template Testing Workflow — Validate Before Deploying

1
Lint

helm lint ./anihpj-chart — Check Chart.yaml syntax, template rendering, and best practices. Catches YAML errors before they reach the cluster.

2
Template (local render)

helm template anihpj-test ./anihpj-chart -f values-dev.yaml --debug — Render templates locally without cluster access. Verify the output YAML looks correct.

3
Dry-Run (cluster simulation)

helm install anihpj-test ./anihpj-chart --dry-run --debug — Simulates the install against the live cluster. Validates API versions and resource types without creating anything.

4
Deploy to Dev

helm install anihpj-dev ./anihpj-chart -f values-dev.yaml -n dev --create-namespace — Deploy to a dev namespace first. Verify pods are running and healthy.

5
Run Tests

helm test anihpj-dev -n dev — Execute test pods to verify connectivity, DB access, and API endpoints respond correctly.

6
Promote to Production

helm upgrade --install anihpj-prod ./anihpj-chart -f values-prod.yaml -n production --atomic --wait --timeout 10m

💡 Never Skip Steps 1-3

On the certification exam, always lint + template + dry-run before installing. The exam tests your ability to catch errors BEFORE deploying. A failed install wastes precious time.

Q1
How do you make a resource conditional (e.g., only create Ingress if enabled)?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

{{ if .Values.ingress.enabled }}...Ingress YAML...{{ end }}. Wrap the entire resource in an if block.

Explanation
  {{ if .Values.ingress.enabled }}
  apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
  kind: Ingress
  # ... full ingress spec ...
  {{ end }}
  # If ingress.enabled = false → entire resource is SKIPPED
  # No empty YAML, no error — just nothing rendered
Explanation

Helm uses if for conditionals: {{ if .Values.ingress.enabled }}...{{ end }}. Wrap entire resources. Use eq, ne, lt, gt, and, or, not for comparisons. Resource-level conditionals are standard practice.

8.9 _helpers.tpl - Complete Naming Convention

Standard _helpers.tpl Pattern
{{/*
Expand the name of the chart.
*/}}
{{- define "anihpj.name" -}}
{{- default .Chart.Name .Values.nameOverride | trunc 63 | trimSuffix "-" }}
{{- end }}

{{/*
Create a default fully qualified app name.
We truncate at 63 chars because some Kubernetes name fields are limited.
*/}}
{{- define "anihpj.fullname" -}}
{{- if .Values.fullnameOverride }}
{{- .Values.fullnameOverride | trunc 63 | trimSuffix "-" }}
{{- else }}
{{- $name := default .Chart.Name .Values.nameOverride }}
{{- printf "%s-%s" .Release.Name $name | trunc 63 | trimSuffix "-" }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}

{{/*
Common labels
*/}}
{{- define "anihpj.labels" -}}
helm.sh/chart: {{ include "anihpj.chart" . }}
{{ include "anihpj.selectorLabels" . }}
{{- if .Chart.AppVersion }}
app.kubernetes.io/version: {{ .Chart.AppVersion | quote }}
{{- end }}
app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: {{ .Release.Service }}
{{- end }}

{{/*
Selector labels
*/}}
{{- define "anihpj.selectorLabels" -}}
app.kubernetes.io/name: {{ include "anihpj.name" . }}
app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
{{- end }}
💡
Naming Convention for Exam: Always use include "FULLNAME" . (not template) in your resource templates. include returns a string you can pipeline through other functions. template writes directly to output and cannot be piped. This is tested frequently.

8.10 Complete Deployment Template for anihpj

templates/deployment.yaml - Full Production-Ready Template
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ include "anihpj.fullname" . }}
  labels:
    {{- include "anihpj.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
  annotations:
    checksum/config: {{ include (print $.Template.BasePath "/configmap.yaml") . | sha256sum }}
    # Forces pod restart when ConfigMap changes
spec:
  {{- if not .Values.autoscaling.enabled }}
  replicas: {{ .Values.replicaCount }}
  {{- end }}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      {{- include "anihpj.selectorLabels" . | nindent 6 }}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        {{- include "anihpj.selectorLabels" . | nindent 8 }}
    spec:
      {{- with .Values.imagePullSecrets }}
      imagePullSecrets:
        {{- toYaml . | nindent 8 }}
      {{- end }}
      securityContext:
        {{- toYaml .Values.podSecurityContext | nindent 8 }}
      containers:
      - name: {{ .Chart.Name }}
        image: "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}"
        imagePullPolicy: {{ .Values.image.pullPolicy }}
        ports:
        - name: http
          containerPort: {{ .Values.service.port }}
        {{- if .Values.probes.liveness }}
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: {{ .Values.probes.path }}
            port: http
          initialDelaySeconds: {{ .Values.probes.initialDelay }}
        {{- end }}
        resources:
          {{- toYaml .Values.resources | nindent 10 }}
        env:
        {{- range .Values.env }}
        - name: {{ .name }}
          value: {{ .value | quote }}
        {{- end }}

9.11 Subchart vs Umbrella Chart - When to Use Each Pattern

These are two fundamentally different approaches to composing Helm deployments. Understanding when to use each is a mark of Helm proficiency.

📦 Umbrella Chart Pattern

ONE chart that declares OTHER charts as dependencies. The umbrella chart owns everything.

anihpj-umbrella/
  Chart.yaml:
    dependencies:
    - name: postgresql
    - name: redis
    - name: anihpj-app
  values.yaml:
    postgresql:
      auth:
        password: xxx
    redis:
      enabled: true
    anihpj-app:
      replicaCount: 3

INSTALL: helm install full-stack ./umbrella
ONE command deploys everything.
All releases share ONE namespace.
🔗 Independent Release Pattern

EACH chart is deployed as a SEPARATE release. They're connected via service discovery.

# Deploy infrastructure first:
helm install postgresql bitnami/postgresql -n infra
helm install redis bitnami/redis -n infra

# Deploy application:
helm install anihpj ./anihpj-chart -n app   --set db.host=postgresql.infra.svc

Each release is INDEPENDENT.
Can upgrade/rollback individually.
Can span multiple namespaces.
FactorUmbrella ChartIndependent Releases
DeploymentSingle commandMultiple commands
RollbackAll or nothingPer-component
Version CouplingTight (one Chart.lock)Loose (independent)
NamespaceShared namespaceSeparate namespaces possible
Best ForSimple apps, demos, devProduction, microservices

9.12 How helm dependency update Actually Works

Understanding the internal mechanics of dependency resolution helps debug "chart not found" and version conflict errors.

1
Read Chart.yaml Dependencies

Helm reads the dependencies array. For each dependency, it checks: name, version constraint, repository URL, optional condition, and tags.

2
Check Chart.lock (if exists)

If Chart.lock exists, Helm compares its entries with Chart.yaml. If they match, it uses the locked versions (reproducible). If they differ, it downloads new versions. If Chart.lock is missing, it resolves fresh.

3
Fetch Repository Index

For each repository URL, Helm downloads index.yaml (cached locally). The index contains all available chart versions with their URLs and digests.

4
Solve Version Constraints

Helm finds all versions matching the constraint (e.g., >=12.0.0 <13.0.0) and picks the highest version. The selected version's .tgz URL is recorded in Chart.lock with its SHA256 digest for integrity verification.

5
Download .tgz to charts/

The .tgz file is downloaded to charts/ directory. These are NOT committed to Git (add charts/*.tgz to .gitignore). Chart.lock IS committed for reproducible builds.

8.11 Building the anihpj Container — Complete Dockerfile

The anihpj/jobpost Django application needs a container image before Helm can deploy it. Here's the production-ready multi-stage Dockerfile.

Dockerfile — Multi-stage Build for anihpj
# Stage 1: Build dependencies
FROM python:3.12-slim AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --user --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Stage 2: Production image
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app

# Create non-root user
RUN groupadd -r anihpj && useradd -r -g anihpj anihpj

# Copy Python dependencies from builder
COPY --from=builder /root/.local /home/anihpj/.local

# Copy application code
COPY --chown=anihpj:anihpj . .

# Set environment
ENV PATH=/home/anihpj/.local/bin:$PATH \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=anihpj.settings

# Collect static files and run as non-root
RUN python manage.py collectstatic --noinput

USER anihpj
EXPOSE 8000

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s \
  CMD python manage.py check --deploy || exit 1

CMD ["gunicorn", "anihpj.wsgi:application", \
     "--bind", "0.0.0.0:8000", \
     "--workers", "4", \
     "--access-logfile", "-"]
Docker Build & Push for Helm
# Build the image:
docker build -t anihpj:v2.0.0 .

# Tag for registry:
docker tag anihpj:v2.0.0 myregistry.io/anihpj:v2.0.0

# Push to registry:
docker push myregistry.io/anihpj:v2.0.0

# Now reference in values.yaml:
image:
  repository: myregistry.io/anihpj
  tag: v2.0.0

# Deploy with Helm:
helm upgrade --install anihpj ./anihpj-chart \
  --set image.tag=v2.0.0 -n production --atomic --wait
class="ckad-practice-drill"> ⏱️ 15 minutes

  2. Chart.yaml: Set name, appVersion "2.1.0", type: application

  4. deployment.yaml: Use template from Section 8.1 with ConfigMap/Secret envFrom

Q2
How do you reference a ConfigMap in a Deployment's envFrom?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

envFrom: - configMapRef: name: {{ include "mychart.fullname" . }}-config. Use include to get the computed name.

Explanation

This concept is frequently tested on the Helm certification exam. The illustration below demonstrates the practical application with real commands and examples you can use directly in the exam terminal.

# Standard install command:
helm install RELEASE ./chart -n NAMESPACE --create-namespace

# Install with values file:
helm install RELEASE ./chart -f values.yaml -n NAMESPACE

# Install with --set overrides:
helm install RELEASE ./chart --set image.tag=v2.0 -n NAMESPACE

# Install with --atomic (auto-rollback on failure):
helm install RELEASE ./chart -n NAMESPACE --atomic --wait --timeout 5m
Q3
What's the purpose of _helpers.tpl?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

Defines reusable named templates (labels, names, selectors). Files starting with _ are NOT deployed as K8s resources. Use {{ include "helperName" . }} to invoke.

Explanation

This concept is frequently tested on the Helm certification exam. The illustration below demonstrates the practical application with real commands and examples you can use directly in the exam terminal.

# template vs include - Key Difference:

# template: writes directly to output (NO piping)
{{ template "mylib.labels" . }}

# include: returns a string (CAN pipe through functions)
{{ include "mylib.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
{{ include "mylib.labels" . | quote }}

# Named template definition:
{{- define "anihpj.labels" -}}
app.kubernetes.io/name: {{ .Chart.Name }}
app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
{{- end }}

# Usage:
metadata:
  labels:
    {{- include "anihpj.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
Q4
How do you pass values from a Secret's data field safely?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

{{ .Values.secretValue | b64enc | quote }}. Secret data must be base64-encoded. Use b64enc to encode at render time.

Explanation

Never store plaintext secrets in values.yaml. Use placeholders, inject at deploy time (--set or CI/CD), encode with b64enc in templates. Production: Sealed Secrets, External Secrets Operator, or Vault.

Q5
How do you render resource limits/requests from values.yaml?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

resources: {{ toYaml .Values.resources | nindent 10 }}. toYaml serializes, nindent adds indentation + newline.

Explanation

Never store plaintext secrets in values.yaml. Use placeholders, inject at deploy time (--set or CI/CD), encode with b64enc in templates. Production: Sealed Secrets, External Secrets Operator, or Vault.

Q6
Where does NOTES.txt output appear?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

In the terminal after install/upgrade. It's not a K8s resource — just user-facing text. Use it for access URLs, next steps, and status commands.

Explanation

values.yaml provides defaults accessed via .Values. Best practices: comment keys, flat nesting, sensible defaults, never store secrets. Override with --set (highest) or -f files.

Q7
How do labels defined in _helpers.tpl get applied to all resources?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

Each resource template includes them: labels: {{ include "mychart.labels" . | nindent 4 }}. The named template returns a YAML block that gets indented into each resource.

Explanation

Files starting with _ are NOT deployed. They contain reusable named templates via {{ define "name" }}. Always invoke with {{ include "name" . }} — never template (no pipeline support).

Q8
What does nindent do vs indent?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

indent N adds N spaces before each line. nindent N does the same but also adds a newline first — crucial when placing YAML blocks on a new line after a key.

Explanation

This concept is frequently tested on the Helm certification exam. The illustration below demonstrates the practical application with real commands and examples you can use directly in the exam terminal.

# values.yaml with documented defaults:
replicaCount: 3
image:
  repository: anihpj        # Docker image repository
  tag: v2.0.0                # Image tag (pin in production!)
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent   # Image pull policy

service:
  type: ClusterIP            # ClusterIP | NodePort | LoadBalancer
  port: 80                   # Service port

ingress:
  enabled: true              # Enable/disable Ingress resource
  className: nginx           # Ingress class name
  host: anihpj.example.com   # Ingress hostname
  tls: true                  # Enable TLS

# Access in templates: {{ .Values.replicaCount }}
# Override: --set replicaCount=5
Q9
How do you reference the parent scope ($) inside a nested range?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

Use $ which always refers to the root context: {{ $.Values.service.port }} works even inside nested range blocks.

Explanation

range iterates lists or maps. For lists: {{ range .Values.hosts }}{{ . }}{{ end }}. For maps: {{ range $k, $v := .Values.env }}. Use $ to access root scope inside range blocks.

Q10
What's the complete workflow for validating template changes before deploying?
Answer & Explanation
Answer

helm lint ./chart → helm template ./chart --debug → helm install test ./chart --dry-run → helm install prod ./chart. Lint catches syntax errors, template/debug shows rendered output, dry-run simulates the install.

Explanation

This concept is frequently tested on the Helm certification exam. The illustration below demonstrates the practical application with real commands and examples you can use directly in the exam terminal.

# Install with values file:

# Install with --set overrides:
